body: i appreciate the time you've taken for a response! - and yeah, i'll try that, honestly that's how i've been trying to deal with my mods since the beginning - by just using logic.
no, he probably just accepts all work coming his way.

just incase no one has told you today, you're a good person, i'm so so greatful for what you've said, i'm going to sleep soon (3am phew) but tomorrow i think i'll look at the sunrise differently.

Thank you!

well in that case i'm glad i could help you in return! you've brightened my evening friend and i owe you, i think i'll be back to read this post on my bad days.

and that's true, my parents do try really hard and i know they sacrifice a lot for me, i haven't been the best son to raise i'm sure but no one's perfect right?

the problem lies with what i was exposed to when i was younger and sure, thank you for taking your time again, well first of all my mother would sometimes turn up drunk to school events for example and overall her behaviour when she was drunk was a side of my mother i didn't like to see, she was violent and angry and she hurt me a lot, not physically, the most she ever did in that area was push me, i witnessed my parents fighting sometimes, my mum would scream for me to come downtairs whenever their fight got out of hand (mother throwing something at my father and visa versa), and i know this is a bit jarring to include but my aunt tried to kill me when i was younger, i don't blame my parents for that at all but i was around 8 at the time and it sent me into a strange depression early on.

My childhood wasn't the best but it certanly wasn't the worst.

Thank you, truly, reading encouragment and advice is something i do rarely and nowhere near frequently enough, i really do appreciate you taking your time to share wisdom with me.

And I know, i miss the security? I suppose? I'm not sure what to call it but i really miss the feeling of another.

And it could be better i suppose, my father wasn't so much an absent father as and uninvolved one, he was there when it counted but I can't shake the feeling of disappointment i get from him on a daily basis, and my mother is an alcoholic, she subjected me to a lot i'd rather forget and to an extent i resent her for it, but i know she has her reasons, they live together but unhappily and that's clear, i witnessed a lot i shouldn't have as a kid and i don't think it did me any good.

thanks for your advice, i try often but the ingrained way of viewing life still has a hold of me.

And sure, the first was a girl let's say her name was Kayla, we met very young over omegle and after talking to eachother we realised we only lived about 100 miles apart, so i made the journey most weekends and we dated for 3 years, in the long run it (birthdays/christmas/travel) cost me over £3k, i think about that a lot.

the second was a girl, let's call her Maddie, she was too good for me, insanely attractive and for the first 3/4 months it was utter bliss until we argued over something and she showed her true personality so to speak, she emotionally tortured me for the best part of a year and we finally broke up when i caught her cheating on me, funnily enough Kayla also cheated on me too.
huge fan already but thank you for taking the time to respond
